data.narrative:
Neuralink is a private-stage AI & Software company that has raised $1.3B+ to date. The target operates within a sector containing 16 peer companies, though the narrow peer set for same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables is constrained—only 1 same-stage company identified, with 0 adjacent-stage and 0 similar-tier peers meeting filtering thresholds. The comp universe includes 1 public company (Palantir, ticker PLTR) and 8 private peers, with top comparables including Waymo, Figure AI, Scale AI, and Reflection AI.

Given the sparsity of narrow-filter peers, traditional peer-median valuation is not applicable; fewer than three datapoints in any single filtered cohort precludes a reliable median calculation. A fallback to all-sector median across 16 AI & Software companies would risk introducing heterogeneity bias, as broader cohort comparables span vastly different business models, maturity stages, and capital efficiency profiles. The single public comp (Palantir) offers a reference point for public-market investor expectations but does not directly bridge to a private valuation given stage and revenue differences.

Absent sufficient comparable-company triangulation, valuation support would require alternative methods—discounted cash flow or venture capital method frameworks—neither of which is supplied in the available data. The analysis cannot responsibly derive a target valuation range without additional revenue, profitability, or cash-flow projections. Key uncertainty remains the absence of bottleneck-stage peers with sufficient commonality to establish a credible valuation anchor.
